unsafe_pattern: A JavaScript/TypeScript test asserts (via assert.match/toMatch/toContain with a regex or exact string) a specific hex color or color-mix() literal value copied out of a themed/visual source file (e.g. docs/components/*.astro dark-mode CSS custom properties), instead of asserting only the structural property (selector exists, variable name defined, contrast ratio computed) that the test is actually meant to guard.
consequence: Every time a human or agent retunes the asserted color for a legitimate visual reason (WCAG contrast fix, palette rebalancing), the test breaks even though no regression occurred, forcing a follow-up PR whose only purpose is updating the literal to match the new value. In this repo this happened twice in a 2-week window: PR #15525 tuned dark-mode colors in docs/components/DispatchIllustration.astro and TerminalDemo.astro, which broke two literal-color assertions in tests/unit/docs-accessibility.test.mjs and tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs, requiring the separate follow-up PR #15538 to update the regexes to the new literals; then PR #15544 (another contrast retune of the same files, same self-care:accessibility-checker workflow) changed --terminal-syntax-placeholder from #ffbe88 and did not update the still-brittle assertion in tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs, so at HEAD (commit 2fefc8f0) `node --test tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs` fails: `assert.match(terminal, /--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffa657/)` no longer matches the current `#ffbe88` value — a real, currently-failing regression the rule would have caught before merge.
mechanical_correction: Replace the literal hex/color-mix value assertion with a structural assertion: assert the CSS custom property or selector is defined with some color value (e.g. /--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}/ or a capture-group-based contrast check), or compute/assert contrast ratio programmatically (e.g. via a WCAG contrast helper) rather than string-matching the designer's exact chosen value. Where the test's actual intent is 'this token still meets AA contrast', assert that computed property, not the literal.
likely_false_positives: Asserting a literal color value is legitimate when the test is specifically about a fixed brand constant that is never expected to change (e.g. a GitHub/Primer base token that is not part of an actively-tuned theme), or when the assertion is paired with a computed contrast-ratio check rather than being the sole guard. The rule should flag literal hex/color-mix matches against files under active visual-design iteration (docs/components/*.astro, src/styles.js) rather than every color literal in the codebase.
existing_plugin_coverage: No published ESLint rule covers this: it requires recognizing brittle golden-value regex assertions tied to a specific pair of source/test files under active design churn, not a generic no-magic-numbers or regex-literal rule that existing plugins (eslint-plugin-jest, eslint-plugin-regexp) target.

evidence.title: Improve dark-mode contrast in docs demos
evidence.detail: Retuned many color-mix()/hex literals across docs/components/DispatchIllustration.astro and docs/components/TerminalDemo.astro for a real WCAG 2.2 AA contrast fix (axe-core violations), including --terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffd1a1 -> #ffa657.

evidence.title: Align documentation contrast assertions with the updated palette
evidence.detail: Follow-up PR required solely because PR #15525's legitimate color retune broke two literal-value regex assertions; updated tests/unit/docs-accessibility.test.mjs's .repository-copy > small color-mix literal and tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs's --terminal-syntax-placeholder literal to match the new values, with no other behavior change.

evidence.title: Improve dark theme contrast in docs hero illustrations
evidence.detail: A second contrast retune of the same two files (--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffa657 -> #ffbe88 and multiple color-mix literals in DispatchIllustration.astro) merged without a corresponding test update, leaving tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs's literal-color assertion failing at HEAD; confirmed by running `node --test tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs` locally against commit 2fefc8f0 (1 failing test, ERR_ASSERTION on the --terminal-syntax-placeholder literal).

evidence.title: Split workflow contract tests by area and fix stale assertions
evidence.detail: Fixed two stale unit assertions reported by the Workflow contracts check (referencing #15576), including updating the terminal color assertion to match the current accessible dark-theme color -- a repeat of the same literal-color-vs-structural-assertion churn previously mined from PRs #15525/#15538/#15544.

evidence.title: Separate documentation contract steps and refresh docs assertions
evidence.detail: Single-line literal-only updates to tests/unit/docs-accessibility.test.mjs (1/-1) and tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs (1/-1) to re-sync the same two brittle color-literal assertions after another dark-mode palette retune; no other test behavior changed.

evaluation.reason: Scratch rule flagging any regex-literal hex/color-mix assertion found 15 sites across 3 files; only tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs:305 (the mined --terminal-syntax-placeholder churn pair, currently failing) is a true positive. 11 other sites are stable, non-actively-tuned literals the mined likely_false_positives description explicitly excludes. Needs a file-scope restriction (docs/components/*.astro under active contrast churn) before adoption.
